name: Stencil Aperture Calculator
blurb: solder paste aperture and area/aspect ratio from pad size and stencil thickness
intro: Paste only leaves the stencil cleanly when the aperture walls are small compared with its opening. This checks the IPC-7525 area ratio (at least 0.66) and aspect ratio (at least 1.5) of the aperture made from your pad, and finds the thickest foil that still prints it.

inputs.label: Pad length (or diameter)
inputs.help: The long side of the copper pad; the diameter for a circle.

inputs.label: Pad width
inputs.help: The short side. Ignored for a circle.

inputs.label: Aperture area vs pad
inputs.help: 100 = aperture as big as the pad. 90 is a common 10 % area reduction for fine pitch; 50-80 for exposed pads (split into window panes).

inputs.label: Apertures of this size
inputs.help: For the total paste volume, e.g. the pins of one package.

examples.title: 0.5 mm pitch QFP lead on a 125 µm foil (IPC-7525 example)
0.4 mm BGA ball pad, 250 µm round, 100 µm foil

usage: Give the pad length and width in mm (diameter for shape=round), the aperture area as a percentage of the pad (100 for no reduction) and the foil thickness in µm. It returns the aperture size, area ratio, aspect ratio with pass/fail against IPC-7525 (0.66 and 1.5), the thickest foil that still passes, and the paste volume. Use it before choosing a foil for a board with fine-pitch parts: the smallest aperture decides the thickness.
sources: IPC-7525B Stencil Design Guidelines, section 3.2 (aspect ratio > 1.5, area ratio > 0.66)
